cards.statement: Amazon GuardDuty automatically consumes CloudTrail management events independently of customer trails.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty receives its own stream of CloudTrail management events. Changing a customer trail's configuration leaves that detection stream independent.

source.title: GuardDuty foundational data sources

cards.statement: Amazon GuardDuty can send newly suppressed findings to Amazon EventBridge for downstream alerting.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty automatically archives findings matched by suppression rules and excludes those findings from EventBridge delivery.
cards.misconception: Suppression hides findings in the console while preserving their downstream alerts.

source.title: Suppression rules in GuardDuty

cards.statement: A GuardDuty administrator can delay initial finding alerts by changing the finding publishing frequency.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty sends initial findings to EventBridge in near real time. The configurable publishing frequency governs subsequent occurrences.
cards.misconception: The publishing frequency also controls the first alert for a finding.

source.title: Processing GuardDuty findings with Amazon EventBridge

cards.statement: Amazon Macie's automated discovery favors previously analyzed sensitive buckets over eligible unanalyzed buckets.
cards.explanation: Macie's automated discovery prioritizes coverage of buckets it has yet to analyze over buckets where it has already found sensitive data.
cards.misconception: Automated discovery concentrates first on buckets already known to contain sensitive data.

source.title: How automated sensitive data discovery works

cards.statement: Scheduled Amazon Macie jobs automatically analyze qualifying S3 objects added or changed since the preceding run.
cards.explanation: Subsequent runs of a scheduled Macie job analyze newly created or modified objects that match its scope, keeping periodic assessments incremental.

source.title: Scope options for sensitive data discovery jobs

cards.statement: Some Amazon Macie managed data identifiers require nearby keywords to detect sensitive data in S3 objects.
cards.explanation: Certain Macie identifiers need contextual keywords as well as a matching value. In structured data, a field or column name can provide that context.

source.title: Keyword requirements for managed data identifiers

cards.statement: AWS Security Hub CSPM cross-Region aggregation automatically enables the service in linked Regions.
cards.explanation: Cross-Region aggregation collects data from Regions where Security Hub CSPM is enabled. The aggregation configuration does not enable the service there.
cards.misconception: Linking a Region for finding aggregation also activates Security Hub CSPM in that Region.

source.title: Understanding cross-Region aggregation in Security Hub CSPM

cards.statement: CloudWatch anomaly detection can account for recurring weekly patterns in a security metric's expected range.
cards.explanation: CloudWatch's anomaly model learns recurring metric patterns. A regular weekly change can therefore fall within its expected band.

source.title: Using CloudWatch anomaly detection

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs metric filters with a zero default automatically emit zero while log ingestion is idle.
cards.explanation: A metric filter's default applies when logs arrive but fail to match. If no logs arrive, the filter emits no default value, so silence is distinct from zero events.
cards.misconception: A zero default proves the event count is zero even when log ingestion stops.

source.title: Creating metrics from log events using filters

cards.statement: CloudTrail event history in a management account aggregates events from AWS Organizations member accounts.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail event history belongs to one account and Region; a management-account search excludes member-account events.
cards.misconception: The management account's event history includes organization-wide activity.

source.title: Working with CloudTrail event history

cards.statement: An active CloudTrail trail records Amazon S3 object access by default for buckets in its account.
cards.explanation: The default trail selection covers management events. Recording Amazon S3 object access requires selecting data events.
cards.misconception: A default trail includes Amazon S3 object-level activity.

source.title: Understanding CloudTrail events

cards.statement: CloudTrail automatically adds an organization trail to new member accounts with the trail's home Region enabled.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail propagates an organization trail to joining accounts in covered Regions, so new accounts inherit its logging configuration.

source.title: Creating a trail for an organization

cards.statement: Member-account administrators outside CloudTrail delegated administration can stop organization trail logging.
cards.explanation: A member account outside CloudTrail delegated administration can view an organization trail but cannot stop or change its logging.
cards.misconception: Local member-account administrators control the organization's trail for their account.

source.title: Creating a trail for an organization

cards.statement: CloudTrail network activity events can capture API requests rejected by a supported VPC endpoint's policy.
cards.explanation: For supported services, CloudTrail network activity events include endpoint-policy denial details such as VpceAccessDenied.

source.title: Understanding CloudTrail events

cards.statement: Amazon Security Lake normalizes logs from native AWS sources into the OCSF schema.
cards.explanation: Security Lake maps natively supported AWS logs to OCSF, allowing consumers to correlate equivalent fields across sources.

source.title: What is Amazon Security Lake?

cards.statement: Amazon Security Lake permits a rollup Region to contribute consolidated data to another rollup Region.
cards.explanation: Security Lake excludes rollup Regions from acting as contributors to another rollup Region, preventing chained aggregation.
cards.misconception: A hierarchy of rollup Regions forwards already consolidated security logs.

source.title: Configuring rollup Regions in Security Lake

cards.statement: VPC Flow Logs include traffic from EC2 instances to the Amazon DNS server.
cards.explanation: VPC Flow Logs omit instance traffic to the Amazon DNS server, leaving a gap in that evidence source.
cards.misconception: VPC Flow Logs capture instance queries to Amazon's DNS server.

source.title: Flow log limitations

cards.statement: Route 53 VPC Resolver query logs can include repeated queries that VPC Resolver answers from its cache.
cards.explanation: VPC Resolver query logging records only unique queries. A repeat that VPC Resolver answers from its cache within the TTL leaves no new log entry.
cards.misconception: VPC Resolver query logs record every DNS query an instance sends, including repeats answered from cache.

source.title: Resolver query logging

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can match transformed events when an active log transformer is configured.
cards.explanation: With an active transformer, applyOnTransformedLogs=true makes a subscription filter evaluate transformed events, keeping downstream selection aligned with normalized fields.

source.title: PutSubscriptionFilter

cards.statement: Disabling AWS STS in a Region can block API Gateway's CloudWatch Logs role assumption for REST APIs.
cards.explanation: API Gateway assumes its CloudWatch Logs role through AWS STS. Regional STS settings therefore affect this REST API logging path.

source.title: Set up CloudWatch logging for REST APIs in API Gateway

cards.statement: VPC Flow Logs requires a customer managed key ARN for an Amazon S3 destination that uses SSE-KMS.
cards.explanation: With SSE-KMS on the flow-log bucket, name a customer managed key by its ARN; a key ID can cause a LogDestination undeliverable error. The key policy must also let the log delivery account write.

source.title: Required key policy for use with SSE-KMS

cards.statement: An organization trail's presence in a member account proves CloudTrail can deliver that account's logs.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail creates member-account trail copies even when destination permissions fail validation; trail presence alone does not establish successful delivery.
cards.misconception: A visible organization trail proves its delivery permissions are valid.

source.title: Creating a trail for an organization

cards.statement: CloudTrail's organization trail role needs permission to write organization-prefixed CloudWatch Logs streams.
cards.explanation: Organization-trail log streams use the organization ID prefix. A role policy scoped to account-prefixed streams misses those streams.

source.title: Role policy document for CloudTrail to use CloudWatch Logs for monitoring

cards.statement: The CloudWatch agent can use different IAM roles to deliver logs and metrics to separate target accounts.
cards.explanation: The agent supports separate role_arn values for logs and metrics. Successful metric delivery therefore does not establish permission for the logs role.

source.title: Common scenarios with the CloudWatch agent

cards.statement: The CloudWatch agent sends EC2 metrics to the instance's Region when its configuration selects another Region.
cards.explanation: For an EC2 host, the CloudWatch agent's configured region selects the metric destination. The instance's Region supplies the default when that setting is absent.
cards.misconception: The EC2 instance's Region overrides the CloudWatch agent's configured metric destination.

source.title: Manually create or edit the CloudWatch agent configuration file

cards.statement: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig automatically selects the Region's existing VPCs for DNS query logging.
cards.explanation: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig sets the destination. AssociateResolverQueryLogConfig selects a VPC for query-log collection.
cards.misconception: Creating a Resolver logging configuration automatically selects VPCs for collection.

source.title: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs can replay subscription events rejected with AccessDeniedException after permissions are repaired.
cards.explanation: AccessDeniedException is non-retryable. CloudWatch Logs temporarily disables the subscription filter and skips incoming logs during that period.
cards.misconception: CloudWatch Logs preserves rejected subscription events for replay after permission repairs.

source.title: Real-time processing of log data with subscriptions

cards.statement: Enabling CloudTrail log file validation creates digests for logs delivered while validation was disabled.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail produces no digest files for logs delivered during a disabled validation interval, even if an administrator later enables validation.
cards.misconception: Enabling validation backfills integrity digests for earlier log delivery.

source.title: UpdateTrail

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation lets IAM roles act as designated approvers for an aws:approve runbook step.
cards.explanation: An aws:approve step accepts IAM role ARNs as approvers. A response plan can therefore assign approval authority through prepared roles.

source.title: aws:approve – Pause an automation for manual approval

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation manual mode lets an engineer start the remaining steps together after the first step.
cards.explanation: Manual execution pauses between runbook steps. Responders explicitly start the next step after reviewing the previous step's result.
cards.misconception: Manual mode gates the first step and then runs the rest of the runbook automatically.

source.title: Run an automation step by step

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation can undo completed containment changes by default when an execution is canceled.
cards.explanation: Canceling an automation does not provide automatic rollback. Engineers define an onCancel workflow for the cleanup or recovery actions their response plan needs.
cards.misconception: Canceling a response runbook automatically undoes its completed changes.

source.title: Systems Manager Automation actions reference

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation lets in-flight targets finish after an execution reaches its error threshold.
cards.explanation: An Automation error threshold stops dispatch to additional targets. In-flight executions can complete and contribute further failures.

source.title: Control automations at scale

cards.statement: Step Functions Asynchronous Express Workflows provide exactly-once execution for containment runbooks.
cards.explanation: Asynchronous Express Workflows use at-least-once execution. Containment actions need to tolerate an execution running again.
cards.misconception: Asynchronous Express Workflows guarantee a containment workflow runs once.

source.title: Choosing workflow type in Step Functions

cards.statement: Step Functions Express Workflows support .sync tasks that wait for a forensic collection job to finish.
cards.explanation: Express Workflows exclude the .sync integration pattern. A response workflow that waits for a supported job through .sync uses a Standard Workflow.
cards.misconception: Express Workflows support job-completion integration through .sync.

source.title: Choosing workflow type in Step Functions

cards.statement: Step Functions accepts task-token callbacks only from principals in the workflow's own AWS account.
cards.explanation: A task token works only when a principal in the state machine's own account returns it with SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure. Tokens sent by principals in another account don't work.

source.title: Discover service integration patterns in Step Functions

cards.statement: AWS Fault Injection Service uses CloudWatch alarms as configured stop conditions in response-testing experiments.
cards.explanation: An AWS FIS stop condition halts an experiment when its configured CloudWatch alarm triggers, placing a measurable guardrail on a response test.

source.title: Stop conditions for AWS FIS

cards.statement: AWS FIS selects tagged experiment targets when an engineer creates the experiment template.
cards.explanation: AWS FIS resolves targets when the experiment starts. Tag changes between template creation and execution can therefore change the resources selected.
cards.misconception: Creating an experiment template freezes its tag-selected target resources.

source.title: Targets for AWS FIS

cards.statement: Engineers can deploy Automated Forensics Orchestrator for Amazon EC2 and EKS in a central forensic account.
cards.explanation: The guidance deploys orchestration components in a forensic account and establishes trust with application accounts for prepared cross-account collection.
tags: Automated Forensics Orchestrator for Amazon EC2 and EKS

source.title: Deployment overview

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation location concurrency caps the resources processed within a target account.
cards.explanation: Location concurrency controls concurrent account-Region pairs. Resource concurrency within a pair is a separate rate control for limiting remediation impact.
cards.misconception: The location concurrency setting limits simultaneous resource changes inside an account.

source.title: Running automations in multiple AWS Regions and accounts

cards.statement: An EBS snapshot of a running EC2 instance's volumes preserves the instance's RAM contents for forensic analysis.
cards.explanation: An EBS snapshot holds volume data only. It excludes data cached in memory by applications or the OS, so RAM evidence needs a separate capture.
cards.misconception: Snapshotting a running instance's volumes also captures what is held in its memory.

source.title: Create Amazon EBS snapshots

cards.statement: A responder who stops an EBS-backed EC2 instance erases forensic data on its instance store volumes.
cards.explanation: Stopping an EBS-backed EC2 instance erases its instance store data. Responders need to acquire relevant local-disk artifacts before stopping it.

source.title: Stop and start Amazon EC2 instances

cards.statement: EC2 termination protection blocks an intruder's OS shutdown when instance shutdown behavior is terminate.
cards.explanation: DisableApiTermination protects against EC2 API termination. An OS-initiated shutdown still terminates the instance when InstanceInitiatedShutdownBehavior is terminate.
cards.misconception: API termination protection also prevents termination initiated inside the operating system.

source.title: Change instance termination protection

cards.statement: A responder can end tracked EC2 connections immediately by replacing the instance's security groups.
cards.explanation: Changing an EC2 instance's security groups leaves existing tracked connections active until they time out. Quarantine rules therefore need a separate way to end those connections.
cards.misconception: Attaching isolation security groups immediately breaks established tracked connections.

source.title: Amazon EC2 security group connection tracking

cards.statement: Deactivating an IAM user's access key automatically revokes sessions already created with that key.
cards.explanation: Deactivating a long-term access key leaves previously issued temporary credentials usable. Responders need to revoke those sessions separately to contain that access.
cards.misconception: Disabling a compromised access key also invalidates temporary credentials acquired with it.

source.title: AWS Security Incident Response Guide: Technique and access containment

cards.statement: CloudTrail uses the same sharedEventID for records of one AWS action delivered to different accounts.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail records with matching sharedEventID values describe the same action across accounts. This helps responders correlate caller-side and resource-owner evidence.

source.title: CloudTrail record contents for management, data, and network activity events

cards.statement: CloudTrail's responseElements value of null proves that a recorded read-only API request fails.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail records null responseElements for read-only APIs, including successful requests. That field alone is insufficient evidence of API failure.
cards.misconception: A missing response payload means the recorded request failed.

source.title: CloudTrail record contents for management, data, and network activity events

cards.statement: Amazon Detective can automatically group findings involving the same IAM role sessions for investigation.
cards.explanation: Detective uses relationships such as shared role sessions to connect findings and entities. Responders use the group to investigate activity across the involved resources.

source.title: Analyzing finding groups

cards.statement: An Amazon GuardDuty Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile finding proves that the detected malware runs on the instance.
cards.explanation: Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile reports malicious files found by a disk scan. The finding establishes their presence, rather than proving that the instance executed them.
cards.misconception: The Execution prefix on a malware scan finding proves execution of the detected file.

source.title: Malware Protection for EC2 finding types

cards.statement: Amazon EBS lets a responder preserve disk evidence at request time while snapshot transfer continues.
cards.explanation: EBS snapshots preserve volume data as it exists when requested. Writes made while the snapshot transfers to Amazon S3 leave that captured disk evidence unchanged.

source.title: Create Amazon EBS snapshots

cards.statement: AWS WAF continues evaluating later web ACL rules after a matching rule uses the Count action.
cards.explanation: AWS WAF's Count action records a match and leaves the final allow-or-block decision to subsequent web ACL evaluation.

source.title: Using rule actions in AWS WAF

cards.statement: AWS WAF can enforce a rate-based rule as a precise cap on requests in its evaluation window.
cards.explanation: AWS WAF estimates request rates and applies rate limiting near the configured threshold. Its rate-based rules do not guarantee an exact request-rate cap.
cards.misconception: Rate-based rules enforce an exact request-rate ceiling.

source.title: Rate-based rule caveats in AWS WAF

cards.statement: An AWS WAF JA3 match can follow a client across changes in its source IP address.
cards.explanation: JA3 is a hash of the TLS Client Hello that identifies a client's TLS configuration. An exact string match on it catches later requests with that configuration, whatever their source IP.

source.title: Request components in AWS WAF

cards.statement: AWS WAF's Continue oversize setting extends body inspection beyond the configured size limit.
cards.explanation: With Continue oversize handling, AWS WAF inspects the body content within the inspection limit. Extra body bytes remain outside that rule's inspection.
cards.misconception: Continue causes AWS WAF to inspect body bytes beyond the inspection limit.

source.title: Oversize web request components in AWS WAF

cards.statement: AWS WAF's Count return override lets a group evaluate rules after its first matching Block rule.
cards.explanation: A rule group's Count return override changes its result at the web ACL level. The first matching terminating rule still stops evaluation inside the group.
cards.misconception: A Count override of the group's returned action converts its internal blocking rules to non-terminating rules.

source.title: Overriding rule group actions in AWS WAF

cards.statement: An unhealthy associated Route 53 check can lower Shield Advanced's mitigation threshold for an Elastic IP.
cards.explanation: Shield Advanced uses associated Route 53 health checks to adjust attack sensitivity for protected Elastic IP addresses. An unhealthy check permits mitigation at lower thresholds.

source.title: Health-based detection using health checks with Shield Advanced and Route 53

cards.statement: Amazon CloudFront automatically interrupts an active download when its signed URL reaches expiration.
cards.explanation: CloudFront checks signed URL expiration when the HTTP request starts. A download that begins before expiration can complete after expiration on the existing connection.
cards.misconception: Signed URL expiration cuts off a download already underway.

source.title: Use signed URLs

cards.statement: Amazon CloudFront can assign native geographic restrictions to individual cache behaviors.
cards.explanation: CloudFront's native geographic restriction setting applies at the distribution level. Different restrictions for content subsets require a different control or separate distributions.
cards.misconception: Native geographic restrictions are configured per cache behavior.

source.title: Restrict the geographic distribution of your content

cards.statement: An Amazon S3 CORS rule directly grants object read permission to callers from its AllowedOrigins.
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 CORS rules control cross-origin browser behavior. Bucket policies and ACLs still determine object access permission when CORS is enabled.
cards.misconception: An allowed CORS origin receives S3 object permissions from the CORS rule.

source.title: Using cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)

cards.statement: AWS IoT Core thing policy variables use the MQTT client ID as the thing name under non-exclusive association.
cards.explanation: With non-exclusive thing association, AWS IoT Core uses the MQTT client ID to identify the thing for policy-variable evaluation. The client ID must match that thing's registered name.

source.title: Thing policy variables

cards.statement: Amazon ECS can vend temporary task execution role credentials directly to application containers.
cards.explanation: Amazon ECS supplies task execution role credentials to its agents. Application containers do not receive those credentials directly.
cards.misconception: Amazon ECS delivers execution-role credentials to the application containers.

source.title: Amazon ECS task execution IAM role

cards.statement: Distinct Amazon ECS task roles create a security boundary between tasks on the same EC2 instance.
cards.explanation: On EC2, task roles do not create container isolation. A container may access credentials belonging to co-located tasks unless additional controls block that access.
cards.misconception: Assigning different task roles supplies a security isolation boundary on a shared EC2 host.

source.title: Amazon ECS task IAM role

cards.statement: In hybrid mode, Amazon Inspector can obtain eligible unmanaged EC2 instances' inventory from Amazon EBS snapshots.
cards.explanation: For eligible instances lacking usable SSM inventory, Inspector's agentless method extracts package inventory from EBS snapshots.

source.title: Scanning Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: With continuous scanning, Amazon Inspector rescans eligible ECR images when it adds a relevant CVE.
cards.explanation: A newly added vulnerability can change the assessment of an existing image. Inspector's continuous scanning refreshes findings for images within the configured coverage period.

source.title: Scanning Amazon Elastic Container Registry container images with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: Amazon Inspector Lambda standard scanning can detect vulnerabilities in custom application source code.
cards.explanation: Lambda standard scanning checks dependencies for package vulnerabilities. Lambda code scanning assesses vulnerabilities in custom application code.
cards.misconception: Lambda standard scanning covers custom source-code vulnerabilities.

source.title: Scanning AWS Lambda functions with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: Session Manager can record commands executed through an SSH tunnel in its session logs.
cards.explanation: Session Manager serves as a tunnel for SSH and cannot log the commands inside that encrypted session; the command transcript is unavailable from its session logging.
cards.misconception: Enabling Session Manager session logging records commands inside tunneled SSH connections.

source.title: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager

cards.statement: An EC2 Instance Connect SSH session stays open after the IAM credentials behind its key push expire.
cards.explanation: IAM is checked when the SSH public key is pushed, not for the session's lifetime. The connection persists until the SSH session ends, so close it or set an SSH timeout on your client.

source.title: Connect to a Linux instance using EC2 Instance Connect

cards.statement: AWS-RunPatchBaseline marks a managed node compliant when its Scan operation completes successfully.
cards.explanation: Scan reports the managed node's patch state. A successful Scan can report missing approved patches; it leaves their installation to an Install operation.
cards.misconception: A successful patch scan establishes that the node meets its patch baseline.

source.title: SSM Command document for patching: AWS-RunPatchBaseline

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can apply a denied-topic policy to user inputs and model responses.
cards.explanation: A configured denied-topic filter evaluates the topics in a user's query and the model's response, helping enforce the application's subject-area restrictions.

source.title: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

cards.statement: ApplyGuardrail runs the application's foundation model as part of checking supplied text against a guardrail.
cards.explanation: ApplyGuardrail assesses supplied text separately from model inference. An application can request that assessment before it invokes a foundation model.
cards.misconception: ApplyGuardrail invokes the application's foundation model during guardrail assessment.

source.title: Use the ApplyGuardrail API in your application

cards.statement: An Amazon EC2 security group reference permits instance traffic across subnets through a routed middlebox.
cards.explanation: Across a middlebox route, instance security groups need the other instance's private IP or subnet CIDR as the source. Referencing its security group does not authorize that path.
cards.misconception: Security group references authorize the source instance even when a middlebox sits on the route.

source.title: Security group rules

cards.statement: An Amazon VPC network ACL can block an EC2 instance's DNS queries to the VPC's AmazonProvidedDNS address.
cards.explanation: Amazon VPC exempts its AmazonProvidedDNS resolver traffic from network ACL filtering, even when a matching deny rule exists.
cards.misconception: A subnet network ACL applies its deny rules to queries sent to the Amazon-provided resolver.

source.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists

cards.statement: AWS Network Firewall still applies its stateful rules to packets that match a stateless Pass action.
cards.explanation: A stateless Pass action ends packet inspection in AWS Network Firewall. Forward to stateful rules is the action that sends a packet onward for stateful inspection.
cards.misconception: Passing stateless inspection still subjects a packet to the stateful rule engine.

source.title: Defining rule actions in AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: With strict rule order, AWS Network Firewall's Drop established default permits TCP connection handshakes.
cards.explanation: The AWS Network Firewall Drop established default lets TCP establish a connection before deciding on application traffic. This makes application-layer pass rules usable in a default-deny policy.

source.title: Managing evaluation order for Suricata compatible rules in AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: For inter-VPC flows on one AWS Transit Gateway, appliance mode automatically pins both directions to one inspection AZ.
cards.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway appliance mode pins an inspection VPC attachment to the chosen Availability Zone for a flow, preserving the return path for stateful inspection.

source.title: How AWS Transit Gateway works

cards.statement: Network Access Analyzer can confirm that an attacker has sent packets along a path reported in a finding.
cards.explanation: Network Access Analyzer infers possible paths from network configuration. Its findings show configured exposure, rather than observed packet traffic.
cards.misconception: A finding from configuration analysis proves that traffic actually traversed the reported path.

source.title: How Network Access Analyzer works

cards.statement: Route 53 VPC Resolver returns SERVFAIL by default when DNS Firewall fails to respond.
cards.explanation: DNS Firewall's default VPC failure mode is closed: when VPC Resolver gets no reply from DNS Firewall, it blocks the query with SERVFAIL, favoring security over availability.

source.title: DNS Firewall VPC configuration

cards.statement: Adding an AWS Client VPN route automatically authorizes authenticated clients to reach its destination.
cards.explanation: AWS Client VPN route tables choose network paths. Separate authorization rules determine which authenticated clients may reach a destination network.
cards.misconception: A Client VPN route also grants destination access to authenticated clients.

source.title: AWS Client VPN routes

cards.statement: With group and endpoint policies defined, AWS Verified Access requires both policy documents to allow a request.
cards.explanation: An endpoint policy adds an access gate to the group policy. AWS Verified Access grants a request when both configured policy documents allow it.

source.title: Verified Access policy evaluation

cards.statement: AWS Network Firewall automatically redirects subnet traffic through a firewall endpoint when engineers create it.
cards.explanation: Engineers insert AWS Network Firewall endpoints into traffic paths by updating VPC routes. Creating an endpoint leaves existing routes in place.
cards.misconception: Creating a firewall endpoint automatically puts it into the subnet's existing traffic path.

source.title: VPC route table configuration for AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: On scheduled secret deletion, AWS Direct Connect changes must_encrypt to should_encrypt after removing the last CKN.
cards.explanation: When scheduled secret deletion leads AWS Direct Connect to disassociate a connection's final CKN, the service changes must_encrypt to should_encrypt to avoid sudden packet loss.
cards.volatilityNote: AWS may revise its automatic response to deletion of the final MACsec key.

source.title: MAC Security in Direct Connect

cards.statement: IAM compares a SAML assertion's Recipient with the role's SAML:aud trust condition during console federation.
cards.explanation: An IAM role's SAML:aud trust condition evaluates the assertion's Recipient value. Matching it to the approved AWS sign-in endpoint restricts where console federation completes.

source.title: Create a role for SAML 2.0 federation (console)

cards.statement: IAM can validate an OIDC JWKS endpoint's TLS certificate through its trusted root CA library.
cards.explanation: IAM normally checks the JWKS endpoint against trusted root CAs. Configured thumbprints remain a fallback, such as when the endpoint's CA is outside that library.

source.title: Obtain the thumbprint for an OpenID Connect identity provider

cards.statement: An STS session's expiration limits the lifetime of an Amazon S3 presigned URL signed with its credentials.
cards.explanation: An Amazon S3 presigned URL signed with temporary credentials expires when those credentials expire, even if its requested expiration time is later.

source.title: Download and upload objects with presigned URLs

cards.statement: Amazon S3 consumes a presigned URL after the first successful use of its authorized operation.
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 presigned URLs permit repeated use while valid. A successful authorized request does not consume the URL.
cards.misconception: An Amazon S3 presigned URL is a single-use authorization token.

source.title: Download and upload objects with presigned URLs

cards.statement: AWS IAM Identity Center revokes AWS account role sessions when a user signs out of the AWS access portal.
cards.explanation: Signing out of the AWS access portal ends the sign-in session. Existing AWS account role sessions continue until their configured expiration.
cards.misconception: Signing out of the AWS access portal revokes temporary credentials already issued for AWS account roles.

source.title: Understanding authentication sessions in IAM Identity Center

cards.statement: The AWS sign-in URL for encrypted SAML console federation includes the IAM SAML provider's unique identifier.
cards.explanation: For encrypted SAML console assertions, the AWS sign-in URL includes /saml/acs/<IdP-ID>. Engineers obtain this identifier from the IAM SAML provider's details page.

source.title: Create a role for SAML 2.0 federation (console)

cards.statement: IAM rejects a SAML assertion when the signing certificate in its uploaded IdP metadata has expired.
cards.explanation: IAM does not act on X.509 certificate expiry in SAML metadata; assertion validity rests on NotOnOrAfter conditions. Engineers monitor certificate expiry and rotate certificates themselves.
cards.misconception: IAM treats expiration of the identity provider's uploaded signing certificate as a federation authentication failure.

source.title: Create a SAML identity provider in IAM

cards.statement: An IAM role session can obtain MFA-authenticated credentials by calling GetSessionToken with its existing credentials.
cards.explanation: GetSessionToken requires long-term credentials from an IAM user or the account root user. Temporary credentials from an assumed role are ineligible.
cards.misconception: An assumed role's temporary credentials are an eligible caller for GetSessionToken.

source.title: GetSessionToken

cards.statement: STS returns an IAM role session's identity despite an identity policy's explicit Deny of GetCallerIdentity.
cards.explanation: STS returns the caller's identity even when an identity policy denies GetCallerIdentity. This makes the API useful for identifying the credentials involved in an authorization failure.

source.title: GetCallerIdentity

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 rejects an IMDSv2 token when a caller uses it to query metadata on a different instance.
cards.explanation: An IMDSv2 token is bound to the instance that creates it. Copying the token to another instance does not authorize metadata requests there.

source.title: Use the Instance Metadata Service to access instance metadata

cards.statement: Amazon Cognito's token revocation makes an unexpired access token fail offline JWT signature validation.
cards.explanation: Revoked, unexpired Amazon Cognito tokens still pass local signature and expiration checks. Cognito's authenticated APIs enforce revocation; those local checks do not query revocation state.
cards.misconception: Cryptographic signature and expiration validation reveal Amazon Cognito's token revocation status.

source.title: Ending user sessions with token revocation

cards.statement: During IAM authorization, a session tag takes precedence over a role tag with the same key.
cards.explanation: AWS STS gives a passed session tag precedence over a matching role tag. An aws:PrincipalTag condition therefore sees the session's value.

source.title: AssumeRole

cards.statement: An implicit boundary deny limits a same-account resource policy's grant directly to an IAM role session ARN.
cards.explanation: A same-account resource policy grant directly to a role session ARN bypasses implicit denies in the permissions boundary. Explicit denies still apply.
cards.misconception: A permissions boundary's implicit deny restricts a same-account resource policy grant directly to a role session ARN.

source.title: Permissions boundaries for IAM entities

cards.statement: A NotPrincipal Deny can directly block a same-account IAM role with a boundary even when the exception names that role.
cards.explanation: NotPrincipal with Deny blocks IAM principals that have permissions boundaries even when listed as exceptions. AWS recommends ArnNotEquals with aws:PrincipalArn for this restriction.

source.title: Permissions boundaries for IAM entities

cards.statement: An IAM user's cross-account AssumeRole requires an identity policy Allow and the target role's trust policy Allow.
cards.explanation: Cross-account role assumption needs the caller's identity permissions and trust from the destination role. Authorization from one account alone is insufficient.

source.title: Grant a user permissions to switch roles

cards.statement: An AssumeRole session policy can grant an action beyond the role's identity policy permissions.
cards.explanation: A session policy restricts the permissions granted by the role's identity policies. Adding an action to the session policy does not expand that grant.
cards.misconception: A session policy supplements the role's identity policy permissions with additional actions.

source.title: AssumeRole

cards.statement: A Step Functions role trust policy can use aws:SourceArn to restrict assumption to a specified state machine.
cards.explanation: Matching the state machine's ARN in aws:SourceArn binds Step Functions' role assumption to the approved source resource, reducing cross-service confused deputy risk.

source.title: Creating an IAM role for your state machine in Step Functions

cards.statement: AWS recommends that a customer choose the ExternalId its third-party provider uses for AssumeRole.
cards.explanation: AWS recommends that the third-party provider generate a unique external ID for each customer. Provider control of that mapping prevents customers from choosing another customer's ID.
cards.misconception: The trusting customer should generate the external ID for a third-party provider's multi-customer role access.

source.title: Access to AWS accounts owned by third parties

cards.statement: IAM Roles Anywhere can map X.509 certificate attributes into principal tags for authorization.
cards.explanation: An IAM Roles Anywhere profile's attribute mappings select which certificate values become principal tags. IAM policy conditions use those values to restrict the resulting role session.

source.title: Attribute mapping and trust policy

cards.statement: An organization-scoped IAM Access Analyzer can flag a resource grant to another member account as external access.
cards.explanation: An organization-scoped IAM Access Analyzer includes the organization's member accounts in its zone of trust. Resource-policy grants to those accounts stay inside that boundary.
cards.misconception: An organization-scoped external access analyzer treats cross-account grants inside the organization as external access.

source.title: Using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer

cards.statement: The IAM policy simulator can verify service support for global condition keys in an identity-based policy.
cards.explanation: For identity-based policies, the simulator evaluates supplied condition values but does not establish whether a service supports the global condition key. Validate service support separately.
cards.misconception: A successful IAM simulation verifies that the target service supports the policy's global condition keys.
cards.volatilityNote: AWS may expand the simulator's service-aware validation of global condition keys.

source.title: IAM policy testing with the IAM policy simulator

cards.statement: Amazon Verified Permissions denies access when a matching forbid policy conflicts with a matching permit policy.
cards.explanation: When both policy effects match an authorization request, the forbid policy determines Amazon Verified Permissions' Deny decision.

source.title: IsAuthorized

cards.statement: An Application Load Balancer can reject an HTTPS target specifically because its server certificate has expired.
cards.explanation: An Application Load Balancer establishes TLS to HTTPS targets but skips validation of their server certificates. An expired target certificate alone does not prevent that connection.
cards.misconception: HTTPS target connections include server-certificate expiration validation by the load balancer.

source.title: Target groups for your Application Load Balancers

cards.statement: AWS PrivateLink enables TLS for a plaintext TCP application by default when engineers create an interface endpoint.
cards.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides a private network path rather than adding TLS to a plaintext application. Engineers configure transport encryption in the application or its supporting infrastructure.
cards.misconception: Creating a private endpoint supplies application TLS encryption automatically.

source.title: AWS PrivateLink FAQs

cards.statement: A CloudWatch interface endpoint with private DNS disabled maps the Regional service hostname to endpoint IPs.
cards.explanation: A CloudWatch interface endpoint maps the default Regional service hostname to endpoint IPs through enabled private DNS. Disabling that setting leaves endpoint-specific DNS names available.
cards.misconception: An interface endpoint redirects the ordinary service hostname even with private DNS disabled.

source.title: Access AWS services through AWS PrivateLink

cards.statement: Amazon S3 can supply the client's private IP as aws:SourceIp for requests through an S3 gateway endpoint.
cards.explanation: For S3 requests through a VPC endpoint, aws:SourceIp is unavailable for bucket or identity policy conditions. Use aws:VpcSourceIp to evaluate the client's private IP address.
cards.misconception: The ordinary source-IP condition key carries the private client address through an S3 gateway endpoint.

source.title: Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3

cards.statement: By default, eligible EC2 instances preserve Nitro instance-to-instance encryption across a middlebox path.
cards.explanation: EC2's default Nitro instance-to-instance encryption excludes paths through virtual network devices. That default guarantee does not cover traffic routed through a middlebox.
cards.misconception: The automatic encryption between eligible EC2 instances extends through an intermediate virtual network device.

source.title: Data protection in Amazon EC2

cards.statement: AWS Verified Access reuses initial HTTP authorization for later requests in the same TCP connection.
cards.explanation: AWS Verified Access evaluates each HTTP application request against its access requirements. A prior authorized request does not replace assessment of the next request.
cards.misconception: Verified Access grants HTTP access for an entire TCP connection after the first authorization decision.

source.title: What is AWS Verified Access?

cards.statement: An S3 bucket policy with Principal "*" can enforce HTTPS for anonymous object requests using aws:SecureTransport.
cards.explanation: An S3 bucket policy Deny with Principal "*" and aws:SecureTransport=false applies to anonymous HTTP requests, including access otherwise permitted by a public read grant.

source.title: Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies

cards.statement: An S3 bucket policy denying s3:* to Principal "*" outside a gateway endpoint blocks console access to that bucket.
cards.explanation: A bucket policy Deny for requests outside an S3 gateway endpoint also rejects public console access. Those console requests carry no matching S3 endpoint ID.

source.title: Controlling access from VPC endpoints with bucket policies

cards.statement: A Network Load Balancer's TCP listener passes TLS through, so the target presents its server certificate.
cards.explanation: A Network Load Balancer passes TLS traffic through its TCP listener unchanged. The target handles the TLS connection and server certificate.

source.title: Listeners for your Network Load Balancers

cards.statement: Amazon EMR application overrides can disable endpoint encryption despite automatically configured transport protection.
cards.explanation: EMR security configurations set application encryption defaults. Application overrides can disable encryption for specific endpoints, so the cluster setting alone does not prove their transport protection.

source.title: Encryption options for Amazon EMR

cards.statement: The Amazon EFS mount helper can use a localhost NFS mount while automatically protecting remote traffic with TLS.
cards.explanation: For a TLS-enabled EFS mount, NFS connects to a local port. The mount helper maintains the encrypted connection from that port to the file system.

source.title: Encrypting data in transit

cards.statement: Engineers can enable S3 Object Lock on an existing versioned Amazon S3 general purpose bucket.
cards.explanation: Object Lock can be activated after an Amazon S3 general purpose bucket exists. The bucket needs versioning enabled before engineers apply object retention controls.

source.title: Configuring S3 Object Lock

cards.statement: For S3 API requests, Amazon S3 infers a governance bypass from the caller's s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission.
cards.explanation: An API, CLI or SDK request bypasses governance mode only when it also sends x-amz-bypass-governance-retention:true. The S3 console adds that header for users who hold the permission.
cards.misconception: Holding the governance bypass permission makes every API request bypass governance retention.

source.title: Object Lock considerations

cards.statement: Amazon S3 rejects a root user's DeleteObject request naming a version ID with active compliance retention.
cards.explanation: Compliance-mode S3 Object Lock protects an individual object version against deletion requests even from the account root user until its retention expires.

source.title: Locking objects with Object Lock

cards.statement: Amazon S3 releases a version's legal hold automatically when that version's retention period expires.
cards.explanation: An Amazon S3 legal hold stays active until an authorized caller removes it, even after the version's retention period expires.
cards.misconception: A legal hold shares the expiration date of the object's retention period.

source.title: Locking objects with Object Lock

cards.statement: AWS Backup rejects lock changes on a populated compliance-mode vault after its grace period expires.
cards.explanation: After its compliance-mode grace period, a populated AWS Backup vault's lock configuration is immutable even to AWS. The protection persists while the vault holds recovery points.

source.title: AWS Backup Vault Lock

cards.statement: Amazon S3 replication leaves SSE-KMS-encrypted objects behind until the replication rule explicitly opts in to them.
cards.explanation: An Amazon S3 replication rule opts in to KMS-encrypted objects through SourceSelectionCriteria. Selecting the bucket's objects alone leaves those encrypted objects outside replication.

source.title: Replicating encrypted objects (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, DSSE-KMS, SSE-C)

cards.statement: For an SSE-C-enabled bucket, Amazon S3 can retain the supplied encryption key for later object retrieval.
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 discards the SSE-C encryption key after processing the request. The reader provides the key again to decrypt and retrieve the object.
cards.misconception: Amazon S3 preserves customer-provided encryption keys so readers can retrieve encrypted objects later.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)

cards.statement: Engineers can copy an encrypted Amazon EBS snapshot under a different AWS KMS key to replace its key dependency.
cards.explanation: Copying an encrypted Amazon EBS snapshot reencrypts the copy under the selected AWS KMS key. Choosing a recipient-owned key removes the copy's dependence on a snapshot sharer's key.

source.title: Copy an Amazon EBS snapshot

cards.statement: AWS Backup can automatically run built-in application health checks during restore testing validation.
cards.explanation: A completed AWS Backup restore test restores the resource. Engineers supply application validation, such as a health check, through a separate workflow and report its result.
cards.misconception: AWS Backup supplies application-specific validation checks as part of restore testing.

source.title: Restore testing validation

cards.statement: AWS Lambda keeps existing unsigned ZIP code running after engineers attach an Enforce code signing configuration.
cards.explanation: AWS Lambda applies code signing checks to new code deployments. Attaching an Enforce configuration leaves the function's existing unsigned code running.

source.title: Creating code signing configurations for Lambda

cards.statement: A client can verify an Amazon S3 multipart upload by comparing its ETag with the MD5 digest of the entire object.
cards.explanation: For multipart uploads, Amazon S3's ETag is not the whole object's MD5 digest. Comparing it with a locally computed whole-file MD5 misidentifies valid uploads as corrupted.
cards.misconception: The ETag of a multipart object is its complete content's MD5 digest.

source.title: Object

cards.statement: Engineers can rotate a symmetric encryption KMS key with imported EXTERNAL material on demand.
cards.explanation: AWS KMS supports on-demand rotation of imported symmetric encryption key material. Engineers import the replacement material for rotation of the existing key.

source.title: Rotate AWS KMS keys

cards.statement: Engineers import matching material separately into each related symmetric multi-Region KMS key with EXTERNAL origin.
cards.explanation: AWS KMS synchronizes the identifiers of imported multi-Region key material across related keys. Engineers supply matching key material to the primary and its replicas through separate imports.

source.title: Multi-Region keys in AWS KMS

cards.statement: AWS KMS key rotation makes a previously exposed data key unusable for decrypting its protected data.
cards.explanation: KMS key rotation changes wrapping key material while existing data keys remain unchanged. A compromised data key still threatens the data encrypted with it.
cards.misconception: Rotating a KMS key invalidates a compromised data key that it previously protected.

source.title: Rotate AWS KMS keys

cards.statement: An IAM Allow alone can authorize a same-account IAM user to decrypt with a KMS key whose policy omits IAM delegation.
cards.explanation: An IAM Allow takes effect for a same-account KMS key when the key policy enables IAM delegation. A direct key-policy grant is a separate authorization path.
cards.misconception: An identity-based Allow provides KMS access independently of the key policy's delegation to IAM.

source.title: Key policies in AWS KMS

cards.statement: Authorized engineers can update a KMS key's policy while its external key store is disconnected.
cards.explanation: A disconnected external key store makes its KMS keys Unavailable, while management operations such as PutKeyPolicy remain usable. Engineers can adjust authorization during a cryptographic outage.

source.title: Key states of AWS KMS keys

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs reserves data protection policy masking for log groups in the Standard class.
cards.explanation: CloudWatch Logs masks sensitive data in both Standard and Infrequent Access log groups. Selecting Infrequent Access still permits data protection policy masking.
cards.misconception: Data protection policy masking is restricted to Standard log groups.
cards.volatilityNote: Log-class feature availability can expand as AWS updates CloudWatch Logs.

source.title: Help protect sensitive log data with masking

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs automatically merges managed identifiers when account and log-group data protection policies overlap.
cards.explanation: CloudWatch Logs masks managed data identifiers listed in either applicable account-level or log-group policy. The log-group policy adds coverage to the account policy.

source.title: Help protect sensitive log data with masking

cards.statement: AWS Private CA accepts authorized revocation requests for unexpired certificates issued by a disabled CA.
cards.explanation: Disabling a CA in AWS Private CA stops issuance while preserving revocation for its unexpired certificates. Engineers can retire the issuer while continuing to revoke outstanding certificates.

source.title: Manage the private CA lifecycle

cards.statement: AWS Private CA can issue an end-entity certificate whose validity period extends past its issuing CA's expiry.
cards.explanation: AWS Private CA keeps each certificate's validity within its issuing CA's, so end-entity and child CA certificates expire no later than their parent. Plan CA lifetimes back from the leaf.
cards.misconception: A leaf certificate's validity period is independent of its issuing CA's lifetime.

source.title: Manage the private CA lifecycle

cards.statement: An SCP's Allow statement grants its listed permissions to IAM users in attached member accounts.
cards.explanation: SCPs set the maximum permissions available in member accounts. An IAM user still needs an identity-based or resource-based policy that grants the requested access.
cards.misconception: An SCP Allow statement supplies usable permissions directly to member-account IAM users.

source.title: Service control policies (SCPs)

cards.statement: SCPs continue to constrain IAM users when their member account becomes a delegated administrator.
cards.explanation: Designating a member account as a delegated administrator preserves its SCP restrictions. That designation does not make it an organization management account.

source.title: Service control policies (SCPs)

cards.statement: Attaching a permissive SCP to a child OU restores IAM user actions that a parent OU's SCP blocks.
cards.explanation: A parent's SCP Deny remains effective in descendant member accounts. A permissive SCP attached lower in the organization hierarchy cannot remove that inherited restriction.
cards.misconception: A child OU's permissive SCP overrides restrictions inherited from a parent OU.

source.title: SCP evaluation

cards.statement: An AWS service can use a member account's service-linked role to perform actions denied by that account's SCP.
cards.explanation: Actions performed through service-linked roles are exempt from SCP restrictions. This preserves the permissions AWS services need to operate on the account's behalf.

source.title: Service control policies (SCPs)

cards.statement: An RCP can deny GetObject to an IAM user outside the organization for an S3 object in a member account.
cards.explanation: RCPs apply to supported resources in member accounts even when external principals access them. An applicable RCP can constrain an external IAM user's access to an Amazon S3 object.

source.title: Resource control policies (RCPs)

cards.statement: An RCP can block a member-account IAM user's Decrypt request for an AWS managed KMS key.
cards.explanation: AWS managed KMS keys are exempt from RCP enforcement. An RCP attached to their member account therefore does not restrict Decrypt access to those keys.
cards.misconception: An RCP's KMS restrictions apply to AWS managed keys as well as customer managed keys.

source.title: Resource control policies (RCPs)

cards.statement: An AWS Control Tower proactive control can reject an EC2 instance created by a direct RunInstances call.
cards.explanation: AWS Control Tower proactive controls evaluate resources provisioned through AWS CloudFormation hooks. Direct RunInstances calls bypass that provisioning path.
cards.misconception: Control Tower proactive controls intercept direct service API calls as well as CloudFormation resource provisioning.

source.title: Control behavior and guidance

cards.statement: Centralized root credentials management lets authorized administrators remove member-account root credentials.
cards.explanation: With centralized root credentials management enabled, authorized management-account or IAM delegated administrators can delete a member account's root password and access keys.

source.title: Centralize root access for member accounts

cards.statement: An organization management account's root user can directly call AssumeRoot for a privileged member-account session.
cards.explanation: AssumeRoot accepts authorized IAM user or role credentials from the management or IAM delegated-administrator account. Root user credentials are ineligible callers.
cards.misconception: The organization management account's root user is an eligible AssumeRoot caller.

source.title: AssumeRoot

cards.statement: Each AssumeRoot call limits its member-account root session to an AWS managed root-task policy.
cards.explanation: TaskPolicyArn selects an AWS managed root-task policy for the privileged session. The credentials permit that policy's selected actions rather than unrestricted root access.

source.title: AssumeRoot

cards.statement: CloudFormation StackSets automatically propagates accounts' security parameter overrides to new OU accounts' stacks.
cards.explanation: During automatic deployment to new OU accounts, StackSets uses default parameter values. Existing account overrides for security settings do not transfer, so a strengthened setting can be absent from the new stack.
cards.misconception: Parameter overrides applied to existing OU accounts become the automatic deployment values for future OU accounts.

source.title: Enable or disable automatic deployments for StackSets in AWS Organizations

cards.statement: AWS Organizations can register a StackSets delegated administrator with deployment privileges restricted to one OU.
cards.explanation: A delegated administrator for service-managed StackSets has deployment authority across the organization. The management account cannot restrict that registration to specific OUs.
cards.misconception: Registering a StackSets delegated administrator supports an OU-specific deployment boundary.

source.title: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions

cards.statement: CloudFormation Guard can validate change-set replacement actions against an organization's preservation rules.
cards.explanation: Guard evaluates change-set data as well as templates. A preservation rule can flag resource replacement before engineers execute a change that affects retained security evidence.

source.title: What is AWS CloudFormation Guard?

cards.statement: CloudFormation honors a Lambda Hook's stack-role exclusions when evaluating a Cloud Control API create request.
cards.explanation: For Cloud Control API operations, a Lambda Hook ignores stack-name and stack-role filters. Those filters scope CloudFormation stack invocations rather than direct Cloud Control operations.
cards.misconception: A Lambda Hook's stack-role exclusions also exempt matching Cloud Control API provisioning requests.

source.title: Activate a Lambda Hook in your account

cards.statement: AWS Firewall Manager automatically evaluates new organization resources against its existing policies' scopes.
cards.explanation: Firewall Manager continues managing policy scope after creation. As new resources appear, it assesses their scope membership and applies the policy according to its configured settings.

source.title: Using the AWS Firewall Manager policy scope

cards.statement: AWS Organizations tag policy compliance reports list never-tagged resources as noncompliant.
cards.explanation: Tag policy compliance reports cover only resources that have had at least one user-defined tag, so never-tagged resources are absent. AWS Resource Explorer with tag:none finds them.
cards.misconception: A tag policy compliance report flags resources that carry no tags at all.

source.title: Report tagging compliance

cards.statement: AWS Service Catalog can use a launch role's EC2 permissions for users who lack direct EC2 creation permission.
cards.explanation: A launch constraint makes Service Catalog assume the designated role for product provisioning. The user needs Service Catalog permissions, while the role supplies underlying service permissions.

source.title: AWS Service Catalog Launch Constraints

cards.statement: AWS Service Catalog uses a shared product's owner-account launch role ARN to deploy in the recipient's account.
cards.explanation: For a shared Service Catalog product constrained by a specific role ARN, the account owning that launch role provisions the resources. The recipient user's account does not determine their location.
cards.misconception: A recipient's account hosts provisioned resources even when a shared product uses an owner-account launch role ARN.

source.title: Sharing and Importing Portfolios

cards.statement: AWS RAM administrators use separate shares to give two resources of one type different managed permissions.
cards.explanation: Within one AWS RAM resource share, a resource type uses one managed permission. Separate shares let administrators assign different action sets to resources of the same type.

source.title: Terms and concepts for AWS RAM

cards.statement: With organization sharing enabled, AWS RAM requires member accounts to accept invitations for shared resource access.
cards.explanation: AWS RAM skips invitations for same-organization sharing when integration with AWS Organizations is enabled. Account administrators still grant IAM permissions for the shared resources.
cards.misconception: Organization integration retains the invitation-acceptance step for accounts inside the organization.

source.title: Terms and concepts for AWS RAM

cards.statement: AWS Config automatically blocks a proposed resource when its proactive evaluation returns NON_COMPLIANT.
cards.explanation: AWS Config proactive evaluation reports whether proposed resource properties meet its rules. Engineers enforce deployment decisions through a separate gate.
cards.misconception: A NON_COMPLIANT result from AWS Config proactive evaluation automatically prevents deployment.

source.title: Turning on Proactive Evaluation for AWS Config Rules

cards.statement: AWS Config automatic remediation can start on a resource that has already returned to compliance.
cards.explanation: Auto remediation relies on a periodically captured compliance snapshot, so a resource fixed after that snapshot can still be remediated from stale results.

source.title: Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config

cards.statement: The management account can exclude selected member accounts from an AWS Config organization conformance pack.
cards.explanation: AWS Config organization conformance packs support an ExcludedAccounts list. The management account can use it to omit approved member accounts when deploying the pack.

source.title: PutOrganizationConformancePack

cards.statement: An engineer can attach remediation directly to a service-linked AWS Config rule using PutRemediationConfigurations.
cards.explanation: PutRemediationConfigurations does not attach remediation to service-linked AWS Config rules. Service ownership limits this direct configuration path, even if the caller has the API permission.
cards.misconception: PutRemediationConfigurations attaches remediation to service-linked rules in the same way as customer-managed rules.

source.title: PutRemediationConfigurations

cards.statement: With AWS Security Hub disabled, AWS Security Hub CSPM requires AWS Config key recording for accurate KMS.5 findings.
cards.explanation: Standalone AWS Security Hub CSPM needs AWS Config to record AWS KMS keys for its KMS.5 resource checks. Missing recording produces warning findings rather than an evaluation of the key configuration.
cards.volatilityNote: Security Hub and CSPM integration has changed how configuration recorders are created and managed.

source.title: Enabling and configuring AWS Config for Security Hub CSPM

cards.statement: AWS Security Hub CSPM automatically marks failed findings PASSED after their control is disabled across standards.
cards.explanation: Disabling a Security Hub CSPM control across standards stops its checks and archives associated findings. Archival does not record successful remediation of the failed resources.
cards.misconception: Disabling a control changes its existing failed findings into evidence of compliance.

source.title: Generating and updating control findings

cards.statement: AWS Artifact's AWS reports can attest that a customer's own security controls meet their compliance requirements.
cards.explanation: AWS compliance reports in AWS Artifact attest to AWS infrastructure, services and AWS-operated controls. Customers obtain separate evidence for their own workload controls.
cards.misconception: AWS compliance reports available in AWS Artifact attest to the customer's own workload controls.

source.title: What is AWS Artifact?

cards.statement: AWS Artifact automatically extends an active organization agreement to accounts that later join that organization.
cards.explanation: An active AWS Artifact organization agreement covers later member accounts automatically. Organization-wide acceptance supplies their coverage under that agreement.

source.title: Managing agreements in AWS Artifact

cards.statement: AWS Well-Architected Tool applies revised workload answers to previously saved milestones during risk reporting.
cards.explanation: An AWS Well-Architected Tool milestone report preserves answers and risks from the time the milestone was saved. Later workload edits leave that historical review evidence unchanged.
cards.misconception: A saved milestone report recalculates its historical risks using later workload answers.

source.title: Generating a milestone report
